events.text: A new season appears to have started around 09:00 UTC on 2026-11-02: player ratings vanished from battle logs at that hour, a new Evolution appeared, and later that day the Path of Legends leaderboards came back empty on all 13 boards.

assumptions.text: A period is the battles played between two data collections. Small ones merge into the next, so periods run from about half a day to several days. The forecast treats hours as hours, so uneven gaps do not stretch its time axis.
assumptions.test: Collect daily at the same hour and compare.

assumptions.text: Only Ranked battles from sampled leaderboard players' logs count, on both sides. This describes top players and their opponents, not everyone.
A battle log holds a player's last 30 battles. After a long gap between collections, the older hours mostly show less active players, which can look like the meta moving.
assumptions.test: Compare hours collected soon after they happened with the same hours collected later.

assumptions.text: Backtests only use battles already fetched at each origin, and score against every battle later seen. A collection that fetched few logs leaves its period thinly known at that origin, which hurts every method in that period.
assumptions.test: Collect full lists on every run and compare.

assumptions.text: The matchup model's strength setting (C) comes from one selection on 2026-10-24, which looked at later battles than the earliest origins. Each origin's weights are still fitted only on earlier battles.

Each model still has the same regular players in training and later battles, so the matchup weights can partly remember players rather than cards. That is why the deck check leads with players new to a deck.
assumptions.test: Refit without the players being scored.

assumptions.text: Win estimates are at equal player rating. Rating does not capture everything about skill: a deck used by unusually good players can still look stronger than it is.
assumptions.test: Compare results of the same players on different decks.

assumptions.text: Estimates average log-odds over the field before turning them into a win chance, which is close but not identical to averaging win chances. The gap is measured and shown.
assumptions.test: Average over real sampled opponents instead.

assumptions.text: Battle logs stopped giving player ratings when the new season started. A battle with no rating gap counts toward usage, but toward no win estimate, record or model, because a skill gap could not be told from a deck's strength. If ratings do not return, the win estimates stop updating.
assumptions.test: Recheck once ratings return to the logs.

assumptions.text: A forecast can only continue what its history shows. A season start, a balance change or a new card has no history here, and no model on this data can see it coming.
assumptions.test: Collect across several seasons, then test a season-level forecast.

assumptions.text: The deck check is fragile. Run on 2026-11-02 while still counting battles with no rating gap as evenly rated, the picks' lead over most played among players new to a deck was +3.65 points (90% range -1.08 to +7.58, not clear). Leaving those battles out, as now, made it clear. A verdict that moves with a data rule should be read as tentative.
assumptions.test: Repeat the same check over more periods, with its rules unchanged.

assumptions.text: Every signal about what makes a deck good is an association. It does not prove that changing that signal would make a deck win more.
assumptions.test: An experiment would be needed, which this data cannot provide.
